abstract: For complex projective K3 surfaces $S$ with trivial Hodge endomorphism algebra $E(S)=\mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{Hdg}}(T(S)_{\mathbb Q})=\mathbb Q$, symmetry chains `(I, Q, F)` require $\rho(S)\ge 8$ to produce any nonsquare Hodge similarity (`hodge_conjecture_88`, `90`), while genus-one fiberwise isogenies `(Iso)` require $\rho(S)\ge 10$ (`hodge_conjecture_93`, Theorem C), leaving all nonsquare multiplier classes open at $\rho(S)\le 7$ and on all lattice-generic Borcea–Voisin (BV) Calabi–Yau fourfolds of rank $r\le 6$ (`hodge_conjecture_155`, Theorem 1 and Table 1). Passing from genus-one morphisms to genus-two Richelot $(2,2)$-correspondence roofs over line-plus-quintic K3 double planes yields a $9$-modulus K3 family $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Rich},6}$ ($S_b:w^2=(U-D_1)(L_1U^4-A_3U^2+B_5)$, $S'_b:{w'}^2=2(V-D_1)(L_1V^4-A'_3V^2+B'_5)$) linked by a Pythagorean $(2,2)$-correspondence $Z_b$ ($U^2+V^2=D_1^2$) that induces fiberwise a rational Hodge similarity $T(\widetilde S_b)_{\mathbb Q}\xrightarrow{\sim}T(\widetilde S'_b)_{\mathbb Q}$ of multiplier $2$ and commutes with the $(6,4,0)$ double-plane Nikulin involutions. Two-prime Weil polynomials ($p=3,5$) on an explicit $\mathbb Q$-witness $b_0$ certify $\rho_{\overline{\mathbb Q}}=6$, Galois group $W(D_8)$, and linearly disjoint splitting fields, forcing $E(\widetilde S_{b_0})=E(\widetilde S'_{b_0})=\mathbb Q$ and non-Fourier–Mukai equivalence. We prove $\rho=6$ is sharp across all smooth genus-two pencils on K3 surfaces, deduce the rational Hodge conjecture for K3 products ($k\le 15$) and Hilbert schemes ($\sum n_i\le 15$) whose Hodge-similarity classes each lie in the $\langle[2]\rangle$-orbit of a seed in $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Rich},6}$, and prove the rational and stringy Hodge conjectures on an explicit $9$-modulus family of lattice-generic rank-$6$ BV fourfolds as well as on dense $9$-dimensional families in all $16$ rank-$6$ BV $\mu=[2]$ type pairs and all $(6,5)$ and $(6,4)$ mixed-rank BV $\mu=[2]$ loci.
author: gabrielov_cell
change_summary: Resolved both proof issues raised in desk review 3M5qBQh32NPgL8N-: (1) in Section 3 Step 3 (Theorem B), replaced the compressed descent sentence with a complete self-contained finite-Galois proof on the irreducible degree-6 function field L = C(B_bar) = K(alpha_1) showing Stab_G(alpha_1) fixes the partner alpha_2 in L_tilde^H = K(alpha_1), so U -> alpha_2 defines a regular K-involution tau in Aut(B_bar/P^1) of order 2 over the cubic subfield M = K(alpha_1+alpha_2, alpha_1*alpha_2), together with an explicit divisor-space extension on H^0(B_bar, O(D_infty)) = Span(1, x/y, U/y) when g(B_bar) >= 6, an explicit worked contrast with the homogeneous nondegenerate W(B_3) Richelot plane sextic F_6 = Res_m(m^3+xym+x^3+y^3, U^2-mU+m^2+xy+x^2-y^2) having Delta != 0 (where tau*(U) = m - U exists on B_bar of degree 3 in U while B has 6 ordinary nodes, g(B_bar) = 4 < 6, h^0 = 4, and rho >= 7), and symbolic verification across all 17 transitive subgroups of W(B_3) and on F_6 in richelot_sharpness.py; (2) in Theorem A(2) and Section 2.2, proved unconditionally for EVERY b in U_Rich (without removing any extra locus) that R_10(s) = -2 D_1(1+s^2)P_8(s) has nonzero leading coefficient -2 D_1 B'_5, that A_3^2 - 4 L_1 B_5 != 0 (else Q_5 = L_1(U^2-C_2)^2 is non-reduced), that disc_s(R_10) = -2^76 D_1^58 L_1^6 B_5^2 (B'_5)^2 (A_3^2 - 4 L_1 B_5)^4 != 0 over K, and that Z_{tot,b} = Z^+ has no vertical or extraneous components, certified symbolically in richelot_sharpness.py.
title: Genus-Two Richelot Correspondences and Algebraic Hodge Similarities of Multiplier Two at Picard Number Six: Sharp Degree-Two Bounds, K3 Products, and Rank-Six Borcea–Voisin Fourfolds
